summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose about 8% to INR48.9 crore while PAT margin fell to 16% from 22.2%, with receivables up to INR64 crore.
summary.overview: Star Imaging and Path Lab's H1 FY27 revenue grew about 8% YoY to INR48.9 crore, with B2B and B2C growing 20% and 21% while B2G was broadly stable. EBITDA fell to INR14.1 crore from INR17.3 crore, with margin at 28.9% versus 38.2%, and PAT fell to INR7.8 crore from INR10 crore (16% margin vs 22.2%). Management attributed the margin drop to upfront human capital, advertising and marketing spend, machine maintenance, and a shift in geographic mix from Uttar Pradesh to Delhi. Working capital absorbed cash: trade receivables rose to INR64 crore from INR49.9 crore and operating cash flow was negative INR6.2 crore, with a large share of receivables tied to legacy COVID-era government dues.

segments.name: B2C
segments.commentary: Grew 21% YoY in H1 FY27; B2C is upfront-paid and management is prioritising it alongside B2B.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Grew 20% YoY; hospital empanelments added 40-45 in the half, taking total tie-ups above 150. Hospital credit terms are 30-40 days.

segments.name: B2G
segments.commentary: Broadly stable in H1 and about 52% of revenue per the analyst's question; B2B and B2C together were about 48% of H1 revenue. Receivables are concentrated here, mainly Delhi/UT government COVID-era dues and UP subcontracted work.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 revenue of roughly INR60-65 crore, implying about 20-25% growth; management said the PAT margin would be sustained at last year's levels.
Medium-term guidance: revenue growth 20-25%, EBITDA margin 30-35% (medium term), PAT margin about 20% over 2-3 years.
Working capital target: achieve flow neutrality (operating cash flow break-even) by end FY27.
FY27 planned capex of INR20-25 crore, mainly equipment and development.
Management declined to give FY28 revenue guidance (analyst floated INR140-150 crore; not committed).
Receivables clarity expected by December end; INR7 crore received in the first week of Diwali.
capex_capacity: Full-fledged diagnostic centre (CT, MRI, ultrasound, X-ray) targeted for commissioning by end November 2026, subject to PCPNDT approval; expected initial annual revenue INR5-6 crore, breakeven within about one year.

Three PPP projects in pipeline (CT, MRI, ultrasound, X-ray); site preparation and machine orders complete, MoU signings pending. Combined capital commitment about INR30 crore for the two projects discussed.
Centre count rose to 26 from 24, including a CT facility at RG Stone hospital in Faridabad.
MRI capacity being added at Tilaknagar; genome sequencing lab under development.
Management said other centres have about 30% spare capacity available for utilisation.
demand_pricing: Management said it bids for B2G tenders only when feasible, and does not match aggressive competitor bids (e.g., 48%, 52% of quoted rates).
Two more B2C centres planned after Dwarka; a couple of B2G tenders in the pipeline in regional markets outside Delhi/UP (Nashik royalty-based B2B model already operating).
Pathology utilisation has significant headroom per management, and B2B partnerships are the lever for pathology growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR65 crore receivables is COVID-era dues and how much is over 6 months old?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bulk of the outstanding relates to legacy COVID-era Delhi/UT government dues, with some subcontracted UP receivables aged 4-5 months. About INR16 crore is more than 6 months old, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Are the PPP projects signed, and what capex and timelines apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Site preparation and machine orders are done; MoUs are pending and the PPP allotment was not publicly announced until MoU signing. Dwarka and the government project are expected to be operational by end of the month; combined capex about INR30 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 revenue and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed H2 revenue of about INR60-65 crore is approximately right and said H2 PAT margin would sustain last year's levels. FY28 target was not committed.

qa_highlights.question: How will the revenue mix evolve, and what are the B2B/B2C targets and cash conversion terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B and B2C will be the focus, with a 50-60% share ratio referenced; EBITDA about 30% and PAT about 20%. B2C is paid upfront; B2B hospitals have 30-40 day terms (30-45 days also cited).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the H2 revenue step-up if B2G was flat in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will come mainly from B2B and B2C, plus new operational facilities and PPP projects once operational.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company stay competitive in tenders and PPP bidding?
qa_highlights.answer: Bids are based on L1 pricing; the company only bids when its own study shows feasibility and does not chase aggressive bids.

risks_watch: Receivables of INR64 crore (up from INR49.9 crore) with about INR16 crore over 6 months; dependence on government and intermediary payment cycles in UP and Delhi.
Negative operating cash flow (-INR6.2 crore) in H1; flow-neutrality target by end FY27 needs to be tracked.
Margin compression (EBITDA 28.9%, PAT 16%) and whether upfront spend normalises to the 30-35% EBITDA range.
Commissioning of the new diagnostic centre (targeted end November, PCPNDT approval pending) and PPP MoU signings.
Management's inconsistent statements on the PPP timing and on whether the B2G share is 48% or 52%; clarify in next quarter.
Management declined to commit to FY28 revenue; watch for guidance.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and the medium-term margin framework, but cautious and sometimes vague on receivables, timing of PPP MoUs, and FY28 numbers, repeatedly declining to commit to targets.
key_quotes: We are working towards achieving flow neutrality by the end of FY27.
We don't go aggressive bidding 48%, 52%, etcetera, what others are bidding.

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 revenue of INR60-65 crore (about 20-25% growth) and a 20-25% medium-term revenue CAGR, backed by one new diagnostic centre due by end-November 2026 (INR5-6 crore initial revenue), an MRI addition at Tilaknagar, and 30% spare capacity at existing centres, though the PPP projects are still pending MoUs and H1 growth was only about 8%.

quality.why: H1 FY27 revenue grew about 8% to INR48.9 crore, with B2B up 20% and B2C up 21% while B2G was broadly stable, but the brief does not state whether volume or price drove this and names no one-off items; the margin compression is cost-side, not growth-side.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to 28.9% from 38.2% and PAT margin to 16% from 22.2%, with management citing upfront human capital, advertising and machine maintenance costs, and medium-term EBITDA guide is only 30-35%, below the H1 FY26 level.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: A full-fledged diagnostic centre (CT, MRI, ultrasound, X-ray) is targeted for end-November 2026 with INR5-6 crore initial annual revenue, MRI is being added at Tilaknagar, and centre count rose to 26 from 24, though PCPNDT approval is pending and PPP MoUs are unsigned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 FY27 revenue of INR60-65 crore (about 20-25% growth) versus H1 growth of only about 8%, driven by B2B (+20%) and B2C (+21%), with 30% spare capacity at existing centres and 40-45 hospital empanelments added in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is planned at INR20-25 crore and two PPP projects carry about INR30 crore combined commitment, but no new major capex has been announced and existing centres still have about 30% spare capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held H2 guidance at INR60-65 crore and declined to commit to FY28 revenue, and H1 growth was only about 8% against the 20-25% medium-term target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Medium-term revenue growth (20-25%) and EBITDA margin (30-35%) ranges are a stretch from H1 growth of 8% and EBITDA margin of 28.9%, and receivables of INR64 crore with about INR16 crore over 6 months could delay cash-linked targets.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A genome sequencing lab is under development and a Nashik royalty-based B2B model is already operating, but no dated product launch was committed on the call.

rows.label: Flow neutrality by end FY27
rows.why: Operating cash flow was negative INR6.2 crore in H1 with a INR17.5 crore working capital outflow and receivables up to INR64 crore from INR49.9 crore, so the target needs collections of legacy COVID-era government dues, with INR7 crore received recently and clarity promised by December.

rows.label: Hospital B2B empanelments and PPP projects
rows.why: B2B grew 20% with 40-45 hospital tie-ups added in H1 (total above 150), and three PPP projects (CT, MRI, ultrasound, X-ray) are in pipeline with site prep and machine orders complete, though MoUs are still pending.

rows.label: PCPNDT approval for new diagnostic centre
rows.why: Commissioning of the full-fledged diagnostic centre by end November depends on PCPNDT approval, which was still pending at the call.

tone.note: Management was confident on B2B/B2C growth, spare capacity and the medium-term margin framework, but cautious and vague on receivables, PPP MoU timing and FY28, declining to commit; analysts pressed on receivables ageing, the B2G share (48% vs 52%) and the PPP timeline.
